Description
Every token a large language model generates depends on data reaching the right accelerator at the right moment. As AI models outgrow any single chip, the network between accelerators becomes the bottleneck that decides how fast — and how affordably — the world's largest models can serve real users. That network layer is what our team builds.
We're looking for an engineer to work at the frontier of disaggregated inference: splitting LLM serving into separate prefill and decode pools and moving the model's KV cache between them at the limit of what the hardware allows. Get it right and users get answers in milliseconds; get it wrong and the fastest accelerators in the world sit idle waiting on data. You'll build components of the high-speed transfer path that make that difference, and you'll learn to measure success in how close we run to the theoretical peak of the machine.
In This Role You Will
Build and optimize the low-level data-movement software that transfers KV cache and activations across accelerators, servers, and heterogeneous memory — over AWS's highest-performance network fabric.
Profile real workloads, find the true bottleneck, and close the gap between "it works" and "it runs fast" — pushing components toward the hardware's limit.
Work across the stack — from network transport up to the inference frameworks — learning from the teams building the chips, runtime, and models.
Deliver features that ship to our largest clusters, for our largest customers, serving the largest AI models in production.
What We're Looking For
Strong C/C++ and a genuine interest in low-level, performance-critical systems — solid command of Linux, memory, and writing fast code.
The instinct to ask "how fast could this go?" and the discipline to measure it.

Annapurna Labs, a crucial part of AWS, is responsible for developing hardware and software components for EC2 infrastructure. Our team focuses on building networking solutions that for Machine Learning (ML) and High-Performance Computing (HPC) workloads on AWS.

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44728.description_preview:
Team:
Chip Architecture
Level:
1-3 years of experience preferred — but we're very open to hiring straight out of school for the right candidate.
Location:
San Jose, CA, USA
About the Role
Broadcom's Thor Ultra NIC product line builds the datapath silicon behind next-generation SmartNICs, including the congestion-control and load-balancing logic that keeps large-scale networks fast and fair under real traffic.
This is a dual role. Day to day, you'll write Network Programming Language (NPL) — our domain-specific datapath programming language, purpose-built for implementing very high-speed packet processing behavior directly on our pipeline — implementing new and existing features on the Thor Ultra datapath. But you'll also work as a junior architect alongside our senior architects: building the behavioral models, doing the analysis, and providing the hardware-feasibility feedback that shapes how features get specified in the first place. It's a strong path for someone who wants to grow into a datapath architect while staying hands-on with real implementation.
What makes the role distinct is that it lives at the intersection of two disciplines. You can't write good NPL without understanding both the networking behavior you're implementing and the silicon architecture and microarchitecture it has to run on. We're looking for someone who is genuinely interested in operating across both — not a pure networking engineer and not a pure hardware engineer, but someone who wants to be both.
What You Will Do
Write and maintain NPL implementing datapath features on the Thor Ultra NIC product line, working from architecture specifications — including support for multiple congestion-control protocols running side by side on the same datapath.
Build behavioral/reference models (typically in Python or C/C++) as architecture-level work under senior-architect guidance: prototyping and analyzing new schemes before they're committed to a spec, giving RTL designers clear guidance on intended behavior, helping the design verification (DV) team build checkers, and unit-testing a new block's architecture before it's exercised in larger, full-chip simulations.
Feed hardware-feasibility findings back up to protocol and system architects — what turns out to be practical (or impractical) to build should shape architecture decisions, not just follow from them.
Work with architects to turn spec behavior (e.g. entropy / load-balancing schemes, state-machine-driven congestion handling) into concrete, testable requirements, and help document and close gaps between specs, models, and RTL as they surface.
Support the software (SW), design verification (DV), and emulation teams by programming and tuning NPL parameters — and other chip-level parameters affected by NPL — throughout pre-silicon verification and emulation.
Play a central role in silicon bringup and hardware debug: bring the datapath up on real hardware, root-cause issues seen in the lab, and drive them to resolution across the NPL, architecture, and hardware boundaries. This is a significant and highly visible part of the job.
What we are Looking For
BS or MS in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
Experience spanning both networking / packet processing and chip-level design or verification (ASIC/SoC, DV). This combination of disciplines is fundamental to the role rather than incidental to it.
Solid fundamentals in digital logic and computer architecture, and fluency in at least one of C, C++, or Python.
Comfortable reading and reasoning about state machines, bit-level data structures, and dense specification documents.
Strong debugging instincts: comfortable digging into unexpected behavior, forming a hypothesis, and verifying it against real data rather than guessing.
Willingness to learn how NPL's logical constructs — tables, registers, functions, and dedicated hardware-accelerated blocks — get compiled and mapped onto the chip's flexible, programmable pipeline (shared bus resources, execution engines, and memory hierarchy). This compiler-driven mapping model is central to writing effective NPL and to reasoning about its behavior in verification and bringup.
Good verbal and written communication skills. Writing clear summaries and documentation — of models, findings, and spec/RTL gaps — is required, everyday work in this role, not an occasional task.
Nice to Have
﻿Hands-on experience with P4, NPL, or another domain-specific dataplane programming language — this matters more to us than general RTL / HDL experience.
Protocol-level experience (congestion control, ECN, load balancing, TCP) and the ability to debug distributed state machines and systems.
Experience with RDMA/RoCE is a significant plus.
Familiarity with AI/ML workloads — basic understanding of training and inference is welcome, and knowledge of collective communication operations is a significant plus.
Experience with RTL/C-model cross-validation or golden-model-based verification flows.
Scripting for test automation (Python) and comfort in a Linux environment.

About Slate
At Slate, we’re building safe, reliable vehicles that people can afford, personalize and love—and doing it here in the USA as part of our commitment to reindustrialization. About Slate
At Slate, we’re building safe, reliable vehicles that people can afford, personalize and love—and doing it here in the USA as part of our commitment to reindustrialization. The spirit of DIY and customization runs throughout every element of a Slate, because people should have control over how their trucks look, feel, and represent them.
Who we are looking for
We are looking for a Manufacturing Systems Support Engineer to be the first line of defense when something goes wrong with Slate’s manufacturing technology stack. This is an entry-level role for someone who is technically grounded, methodically under pressure, and comfortable working on the factory floor alongside operators and supervisors as well as with software engineers and IT. You will diagnose and resolve issues across MES, WMS, CMMS, and their integrations — reading logs, querying data, following a hypothesis, and escalating with precision when you reach the limits of your access. If you are energized by troubleshooting real problems in a fast-moving environment and want to build deep expertise in how manufacturing software systems work, this is where that career starts.
What you get to do
Serve as the first point of contact for manufacturing system issues — triage incoming requests from operators, supervisors, and quality engineers across MES, WMS, and CMMS.
Diagnose software issues by reading application logs, querying databases, and tracing data flows to isolate whether a problem is a user error, a configuration issue, a data integrity problem, or a software defect.
Follow established troubleshooting runbooks to resolve known issue patterns; document any gaps or improvements you discover so the knowledge base stays accurate and genuinely useful.
Escalate to the software engineering team when an issue requires a code fix — write precise escalation tickets that include what you observed, what you ruled out, and what data supports your conclusion.
Monitor system health dashboards and act on anomalies before they become production-stopping events; know what normal looks like so you can recognize when something isn’t.
Analyze incident data to identify recurring patterns and high-frequency issue types — surface these trends to the engineering team with supporting data to drive permanent fixes rather than repeated workarounds.
Manage user administration tasks including account setup, access provisioning, and permission changes across manufacturing system platforms.
Support software release activities — execute test scripts, validate deployments against expected behavior, and flag regressions before they reach the production floor.
Walk the floor when the problem requires it — some issues only make sense when you see them in context at the station where they are happening.
What you bring to the team
Technical Skills
0–3 years of experience in IT support, helpdesk, technical operations, or a related role; exposure to manufacturing or industrial systems is a bonus but not expected.
Able to read and interpret application logs to distinguish a user error from a misconfiguration from a software defect — the error message is the starting point, not the answer.
Basic SQL: able to write straightforward queries to look up records, verify data integrity, cross-reference tables, and support incident investigation without needing a developer to pull the data for you.
Working understanding of how web-based software systems operate — browsers, REST APIs, databases, and how requests flow between them — sufficient to trace where in a stack something went wrong.
Experience using an ITSM ticketing system such as ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, Zendesk, or similar to manage and document support work.
Comfortable working in both Windows and Linux environments at an operator and configuration level.
Familiarity with monitoring or observability dashboards such as Grafana, Zabbix or Datadog is a plus.
Basic scripting ability in Python, Bash, or similar — not required, but valued and a strong indicator of the curiosity this role rewards.
How You Work
Methodical troubleshooter: you form a hypothesis, test it, confirm or rule it out, and move to the next one. You do not randomly change things hoping the problem goes away.
Clear communicator under pressure: when a production line is down, you can tell a supervisor what you know, what you are doing, and what you do not know yet — all in plain language, without adding to the panic.
Owns the ticket to closure: you do not close an issue until you have confirmed it is resolved, not just until the user stopped responding. Verified resolution is the bar.
Curious about root causes: “It’s working now” is not an acceptable end state when you do not know why it failed. You document what you found even when you cannot yet explain it, because that note prevents the next incident.
Comfortable on the floor: manufacturing environments are active and sometimes loud. You are willing to walk out to a station and observe a problem firsthand when context would help you diagnose it faster.
Keeps learning: manufacturing systems are broad and deep. You do not need to know everything on day one, but you should want to understand something new every week.
Experience And Education
Associate or bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, or a related field — or equivalent hands-on experience that demonstrates the same capabilities.
Manufacturing or industrial environment experience is welcomed but not required for a candidate with strong fun

Join Us, and Ship Robots
Weave was founded to build the robots we’d want to have in our own home. We believe the next generation of robotics will transform everyday life by enabling people to do more and to reclaim time to spend on what’s important.
We also believe robots are in a sense like any other product: to matter, they have to ship. Our robots are already operating in real homes and businesses, giving us the opportunity to rapidly improve from real-world experience. With a growing team, strong customer demand, and capital for expansion, we’re entering an exciting stage of growth—and we’re looking for people with exceptional talent and standards to help bring home robotics to millions of households.
The Role
Simulation is essential at nearly every level of our stack: validating kinematics, iterating on controls research, stress testing new mechanisms, trying new manipulation strategies, and proving out the robustness of our planning and SLAM stack. How fast all of those loops run, and how honestly simulation predicts hardware, is decided by the software this role owns.
You'll build our simulation platform as a core product with customers across the company: the environments, the models, and the fidelity work that makes "it works in sim" mean something.
Responsibilities
Own the sim stack. Isaac Lab, MuJoCo, or equivalent: environments, assets, robot models, and the tooling around them, kept current with every hardware revision that ships.
Model what matters. Actuator models (torque limits, friction, thermal behavior) and contact parameters identified against dyno and robot data with the motor control and controls teams; you know which fidelity buys transfer and which buys nothing.
Make training fast. GPU-parallel environment throughput, profiling, and the determinism and seeding discipline that make experiments reproducible.
Serve sim-to-real. System-identification pipelines, domain randomization tooling, and honest side-by-side measurement of where simulation and hardware disagree.
Catch regressions before hardware does. Scenario and regression suites that run controllers and policies in sim on every change.
Keep assets true. The pipeline from CAD and robot description to sim-ready assets, so simulation tracks the robot we actually build.
What You'll Bring
3+ years building simulation or robotics software, with deep hands-on experience in at least one modern robotics simulator (Isaac Lab/Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, Drake, or similar).
Physics literacy: knowledge of contact solvers, fabrics solvers, integrators, and friction models, including the specific limits of each.
Strong Python and C++ and the engineering habits to make a research-facing platform reliable.
Performance skill: you've profiled and scaled GPU-parallel workloads and treat environment throughput as a feature.
Respect for the real robot. You've compared sim to hardware honestly and changed the sim.
Nice to Have
RL training experience: you've been the customer of a sim stack and remember what hurt.
Rendering or synthetic-data experience for perception training.
USD or asset-pipeline experience at scale.

As a Systems Software Engineer focused on the OS, you'll own the OS layer and the IPC layer that connects it all: the kernel and its real-time behavior, scheduling, memory management, user-space drivers, time synchronization, and the shared-memory transport that moves data between processes with minimal copies and bounded latency. You'll also own how the system operates unattended: boot, OTA updates with rollback, service supervision, crash capture, and health monitoring.
Your software is the layer every other team builds on, and it ships on every robot. When new hardware arrives, you'll bring it up alongside electrical, controls, and robotics engineers.
Responsibilities
System architecture: Design and implement the core systems that every robotics application depends on, including on-device and remote networking, IPC, scheduling, synchronization, and resource management.

Design for reliability: Build diagnostics, health monitoring, and fault-handling systems that improve robot robustness and serviceability.
Debug across the stack: Investigate issues spanning hardware, firmware, and robotics software.

Deep Linux internals: 3+ years working at the OS level. Schedulers, memory, filesystems, and the kernel/userspace boundary.
Modern C++: Strong proficiency developing production-quality C++ software for embedded or real-time systems.
Systems programming: Strong understanding of Linux systems programming, including threading, synchronization, memory management, IPC, scheduling, and performance optimization, along with experience with the embedded Linux stack, including U-Boot, device trees, kernel configuration, DMA, and Buildroot or Yocto.
Hardware/software debugging: Comfortable reading schematics, probing hardware with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, and debugging issues that span electrical, firmware, and software boundaries. Experience using tools like gdb, strace, ltrace and others to understand system behavior.
Nice to Have
Experience with Embedded Linux platform work: U-Boot, device trees, kernel config, DMA and the like.
Experience with secure boot, firmware update systems, or OTA infrastructure.
Experience with microcontrollers, device drivers, peripherals, board support packages, and custom hardware bring-up.
Experience with Rust is a plus.

A platform can be powerful and still fail if people don't enjoy using it. The surfaces developers interact with directly often dictate whether they stick around, no matter what happens underneath the hood. Building a product experience that's powerful, reliable, and genuinely enjoyable to use is still the domain of very talented humans, and we want you to be one of them.
The Team:
Convex has assembled a team of engineers who have built and designed some of the largest platforms in the world, with exabytes of data, millions of transactions per second, and shipped desktop and mobile software onto billions of devices. We are a group of friendly, collaborative, and passionate people that love working in-person together in our office in San Francisco. We hire primarily in SF but have a few experienced folks working remotely in certain situations.
The Role:
Convex’s product surface area is vast and includes our dashboard, insights, third-party integrations, project management, and more. These surfaces are core to our customers' businesses and need to be both powerful and delightful to use. We're looking for engineers who are deeply passionate about building good product experiences, especially as we grow more up-market.
This isn't a role for people who just want to solve puzzles. You'll apply product sensibilities to deciding "why" and "what" we build, not just "how". If you're an engineer with good design taste who cares about quality and enjoys working directly with customers to understand what they actually need, you'll likely be a great fit for this team.
What You’ll Do:
Design, build and maintain Convex's platforms, dashboard UI, integrations, and other services.
Work directly with customers and company leadership (hi! this is me, James) to shape plans for what features we need to build.
Projects you may work on in your first few months at Convex:
Design and build UIs for Convex Backend Components
Enhancing Convex's dashboard, CLI, and MCP to be world-class for AI agents
Upgrading Convex's role-based access control system to allow access tokens and integrations to have finer-grained permissions
What Excites Us:
Strong UX sensibilities and enthusiasm to build intuitive interfaces.
The ability to conceptualize the needs of someone else. Often our customers have much larger teams than ours with different business requirements we need to understand.
Experience or enthusiasm for scaling in a high growth startup environment.
Interest to work in-person at Convex's office in SF.
An ability to write high quality code and an enthusiasm for not being constrained to a certain layer of the stack
Ideal characteristics
This is an attempt to outline some characteristics of candidates that would make great engineers at Convex. We’re have a high demand for conceptual thought and architectural sensibilities, while also having the typical demands of a small startup.
Have they seen excellence?
If someone has a few years of experience it’s extremely valuable for them to have worked closely with a person, team or organization that’s truly
excellent
, in any domain. Excellence can’t just be learned passively since it requires being better than the status quo. The candidate doesn’t need to be excellent yet but they need to have an appreciation that it requires a lifetime of dedication.
Are they a deep thinker?
Convex is a rejection of industry norms and a belief there’s a better way of building apps. This requires us to think for ourselves and chart our own course. Engineers here need to think deeply about
why
they’re solving problems and the long-term implications of their choices. If someone does something just because they were told to or because it’s a “best practice” they will probably not excel here.
Are they obsessed with craft?
Craft is the difference between something that technically works and something people actually love to use, and it's most of what separates a good developer platform from a great one. We want an engineer who sweats the details most people would let slide, holds a high bar for how things feel to build with, and takes real pride in getting that last 10% right.
Do they value simplicity and pragmatism?
Simplicity is at the heart of all good systems, especially those that are able to scale and adapt to future needs. In addition to architectural simplicity, we also try to
do
the simplest thing to solve a given problem at Convex. Don’t come here because you want to write a consensus protocol or storage engine, even though sometimes we need to do these things. Come here because you want to get really good at achieving great things in the simplest possible way.
Do they bring energy to the room?
Startups are hard. Building something from nothing is hard. Driving forward progress despite uncertainty is hard. Shitting on stuff is easy and just brings everyone else down. We have a high bar for quality but also a high bar for being constructive, positive, and excited about making things better. We’re meant to be having fun here.
Do they have tenacity?
Working at Convex is rewarding and the workload isn’t crazy but our users come first and sometimes that means we need to be on-call. We sometimes (rarely), get paged at night and have to respond with dedication, sometimes need to dig deep to debug a tricky issue or solve a problem no one has solved before. There’s a camaraderie that comes from being in a team where everyone has tenacity, will step in to help each other out, and can be trusted to do the right thing.

About the Role
Regara is a clinical and regulatory intelligence platform for the life sciences industry. Device, pharma, and biotech companies use us to plan and prepare what they need to bring a product to market — regulatory strategy, clinical protocols, study reports, and submission dossiers — across multiple markets.
AI is the product. We run a platform of autonomous agents that research live data, reason over it, and draft complete technical documents end to end. That makes quality a genuinely hard problem. The output is generated rather than fixed, the same input can produce different text twice, and the artifact at the end is a document a customer files with a regulator.
What makes this different from most QA work.
A defect here is not a misaligned button. It is a wrong number, an unsupported claim, or a citation whose source does not say what it is cited for. A generated document can be fluent, well formatted, and wrong — and nothing on the screen will tell you. Catching those before a customer does is the job.
This is a dedicated quality role. You are not being hired to write product features between test cycles; you are being hired because the hardest quality problem at this company needs someone whose full attention is on it. You will own a test surface end to end — from exploratory passes and the cases you write, through the defect trail, to confirming the fix in production.
What You Will Actually Work On
1. Exploratory and Functional Testing
Use the product the way a customer would, then go looking for the places it gives way.
Run functional and UI/UX passes across dispatch flows, result views, and admin tooling.
Probe the edges — empty states, oversized inputs, interrupted runs, permissions, and browser and viewport differences.
Test the workflows customers actually run, not just the screens in isolation.
Re-test each release and catch what regressed.
2. Test Design and Regression Coverage
Turn what you learn into something repeatable that outlives any one release.
Write and maintain test cases and checklists covering core user workflows.
Own the regression suite the team runs before a release, and keep it current as the product changes.
Map coverage against the product surface and say plainly where the gaps are.
Prioritize by risk, not by what is easy to test. A thorough suite over the low-stakes surface and nothing over the high-stakes one is worse than no suite, because it looks like coverage.
3. Verifying Generated Output
The most interesting half of this job, and the part with no established playbook.
Check generated deliverables for internal consistency — numbers, cross-references, section completeness, and formatting.
Resolve identifiers and references an agent produces back against the source of record.
Flag unsupported claims, mismatched attributions, and citations whose content does not support the statement citing them. Citation integrity is the highest-stakes quality attribute this product has.
Grade output against golden examples and feed the results back into the eval suite.
Design test approaches that work when the output is nondeterministic — where "did it produce the expected string" is the wrong question.
4. Defect Reporting and Triage
A bug report is a deliverable. Write it so someone can act on it without asking you a follow-up question.
Isolate a minimal, reliable reproduction — not "it sometimes breaks."
Report with repro steps, expected versus actual, environment, and a severity you can defend.
Trace a defect back to the requirement or workflow it breaks.
Distinguish a code bug from a model-quality issue. They go to different people and get fixed differently, and misrouting one wastes everybody’s week.
Follow each one through to verification of the fix.
5. Release Verification and Quality Signal
Someone has to be able to say whether a release is safe, and be right.
Run release verification and give a clear, evidence-backed read on whether a build is ready.
Track quality signal over time — defect trends, escape rate, and where in the product problems keep originating.
Report quality status to engineering in writing, including the parts nobody wants to hear.
Raise the alarm early when a release is trending badly. A late warning is barely better than none.
6. Test Automation
Move the checks you run by hand into checks that run themselves — where the payback is real.
Extend backend coverage in pytest and frontend coverage in Vitest and React Testing Library.
Write browser-level end-to-end checks for the highest-traffic workflows.
Keep suites wired into GitHub Actions so failures surface on the pull request rather than after merge.
Automate judiciously. A brittle suite nobody trusts costs more than the manual pass it replaced.

Frontend:

AI:
Frontier LLM APIs (Claude), MCP tool servers, RAG, eval harnesses and golden-output graders
Infra:
AWS (ECS/EC2, ECR, SQS, S3), Docker, GitHub Actions
You are not expected to know all of it. Most of your testing runs against the application rather than the codebase — but this is what you will be reading when you chase a bug to its source, and what you will be writing when you extend the automated suites.

US / Iowa Preferred
Full-time contractor, with potential to transition to FTE
Build close to the problem. Learn the whole system.
SureHost is an early-stage hospitality technology company building new ways for short-term rental operators to run and grow their businesses.
Our technical and AI team is based in Pune. Our customer and product team is based in Des Moines, Iowa. We are building the company across both.
Pune is not a downstream engineering center at SureHost. Our India-based technical leaders are company owners and help shape our architecture, technical direction, and strategy.
We are looking for an AI Engineer who already knows how to build and wants to develop a much broader technical range.
You will work directly with two experienced technical leaders—one with deep AI and architecture expertise and one with broad CTO-level engineering experience—while building systems being shaped by our first paying customers.
This is an individual-builder role.
You will write code. You will ship systems. You will also get close to the customer problems, product decisions, architecture, and technical tradeoffs behind what gets built.
What you’ll build
Our AI work spans video and image analysis, multimodal models, LLMs, agents, evaluation, data, and the services that connect those systems to the product.
You Will
Build and improve AI/ML systems using Python
Implement and test LLM, computer-vision, multimodal, and agentic workflows
Evaluate and integrate open-source models and third-party AI APIs
Create datasets, evaluation pipelines, and automated tests
Analyze model outputs and find where accuracy or reliability breaks down
Build data-processing pipelines, APIs, and backend services
Take experiments that work in a demo and make them hold up inside a real product
Debug production problems and improve latency, reliability, and cost
Work directly with technical leadership as architecture and product decisions are made
Learn how customer problems become requirements and technical decisions
Take increasing ownership of systems from initial problem through production
Requirements will change as we learn from customers.
Part of the job is understanding what changed, why it matters, and what should happen next.
What we’re looking for
This Role Is Likely a Fit For Someone With
2–5 years of software engineering, ML engineering, or applied AI experience
Strong Python development skills
Practical experience with AI/ML frameworks and APIs
Experience with LLMs, computer vision, or multimodal AI
Working knowledge of APIs, databases, Git, testing, and cloud environments
Experience turning prototypes into maintainable software
A systematic approach to evaluating AI output—not just deciding whether a demo looks good
Strong problem-solving and communication skills
Curiosity about the customer and business problem behind the technical work
The desire to own more than one narrow layer of a system
Experience deploying AI applications, building agents, working with video or multimodal models, or contributing to production ML systems is a plus.
A different path for an engineer
The goal is not simply to get better at implementing AI features.
It is to develop the judgment to understand what should be built, how the system should be designed, what tradeoffs matter, how it behaves in production, and whether it solves the customer's actual problem.
That happens by staying close to the work.
At SureHost, engineers can move between experimentation, architecture, product questions, production problems, and customer learning because there are very few layers separating them.
You will still be an individual builder.
You will simply get to see—and increasingly own—more of the system around what you build.
What you’re joining
SureHost is working with its first paid customer pilot and preparing for broader U.S. expansion.
That means much of the product still has to be figured out.
For the right engineer, that is the opportunity.
There is no large organization deciding everything upstream and handing implementation downstream. The Pune and U.S. teams work together around the same customer problems and product.
This role begins as a full-time contractor engagement, with the potential to transition into a full-time employee role as SureHost grows.
Build with us
If the goal is to stay inside one narrow technical lane, there are easier places to do that.
If the goal is to understand more of the problem, more of the system, and more of the decisions behind what gets built, we should talk.

We're looking for a highly hands-on AI Engineer to take ownership of building and deploying internal AI capability. This is not a strategy, advisory, or people-management role — it's a builder role.
You'll work directly with senior leadership and employees across the firm to understand how work is currently performed, identify opportunities for automation, and build AI agents and applications that remove repetitive work. An example: understanding how an investment associate monitors portfolio companies, then building an AI-powered system to automate the research, data collection, analysis and reporting involved.
Initially your focus will be the firm's management company and a small, close-knit team. Longer term, there's significant potential to expand AI capabilities across the firm's portfolio companies — for someone who delivers, there's no predefined ceiling on this role.
What You'll Do
Work directly with senior leadership on bottlenecks and repetitive processes
Translate business problems into clearly defined technical solutions
Design, build and deploy production-grade AI agents and applications
Build agentic workflows involving reasoning, retrieval, data processing and interaction with internal systems
Integrate LLMs with existing applications, documents, databases and third-party platforms
Build retrieval/knowledge systems (RAG) for internal company information
Implement evaluation, monitoring and observability for AI systems in production
Design human-in-the-loop processes where full automation isn't appropriate
Establish controls around data access, permissions and sensitive information
Measure impact — time saved, adoption, productivity gains

Accounts receivable, payment matching, collections and exception handling.
Management fee calculations, invoicing and reconciliations.
Expense management and transaction coding.
Month-end close and management reporting.
Cash forecasting, budgeting and financial analysis.
Controls, approvals, monitoring and audit trails around automated workflows.
You’ll work with existing systems including QuickBooks, Ramp, Allvue and Chronograph, taking solutions from initial business requirement through to production.
What We're Looking For
Strong software engineering skills, ideally with significant Python experience
Experience building production applications using LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar)
Experience building AI agents and multi-step agentic workflows
RAG, embeddings, semantic search, vector databases
API development, backend/service architecture
Cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure/GCP) and containerization (Docker)
Comfort designing reliable systems around non-deterministic AI models
A builder mentality: you'd rather ship a working prototype than write a deck about what could be built
Comfort operating with significant autonomy and ambiguity
Strong communication — able to explain technical concepts to non-technical senior stakeholders
Experience with LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex or similar is useful, but we care more about your ability to design robust systems than any specific framework.
Why This Role
This is a rare opportunity to build an AI function from the ground up, with direct access to senior leadership and no legacy platform to inherit. The initial mandate is focused — deliver measurable value for the management company — but the trajectory is open-ended, with real potential to extend into the firm's wider portfolio!
A couple of important requirements:
this is an on-site role in Waltham, MA, and the firm is unable to provide visa sponsorship. Candidates must therefore already have unrestricted US work authorization as either a US Citizen or Green Card holder and be able to work on-site in Waltham
